pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts existing rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test stars one item and asserts the exact list, with ★ on that item only. src/index.js `item` renders the ★.
'AC-3' stars items 3 and 1 and asserts only those two are listed, in id order. The query uses ORDER BY id.
'AC-4' checks both `/` and `/?show=all` list all items in id order.
'AC-5' asserts the exact link markup on both views.
'AC-6' sends 'Starred', 'none', an empty value and '__proto__' and asserts 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. The 'AC-7' test asserts it, and the traffic Worker appends the path to the URL, so the query is preserved.

findings.what: The 'No starred items' state test was loosened in the last commit (8e37cce, 'Follow-up edits'). `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `expect(listed(html)).toBeDefined()`, which can never fail, because `listed` always returns an array. The state table row 'No starred items → list shows nothing' is no longer checked. A bug that listed items alongside the message would pass. The spec gives no justification for loosening it.
The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and only mentions the traffic fake app change. The final commit did loosen an assertion, so the claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and re-check the claim, or disclose the loosening and its reason.

findings.what: The route regex now accepts a '?' anywhere after the leading '/', so it also allows routes like '/?'. The change is intended and tested, but the error message still says only 'paths starting with "/"'.
findings.fix: Optionally mention that a query string is allowed in the message.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. The decisions (starred items keep their place; the view is a query parameter) are followed in src/index.js. The spec file was not edited after the go.
All seven acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. The 'No starred items' state-table row has a test, but its list-empty assertion was gutted.
The tests are mostly behavioural. The last commit weakened the 'No starred items' test to an assertion that can never fail. I did not run the tests here. CI runs them.
README mentions ?show=starred. The change is small and the doc is accurate.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so '__proto__' is handled. The SQL fragment comes from a fixed map, not from user input.
The `show` parameter is validated against an allow-list. The query has no user-controlled SQL. Titles are escaped. I found no planted instructions.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and there are no stylesheets or components.
There is no browser flow or screenshot, and the page is plain server-rendered HTML.
The title is within 72 characters and describes the change. The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false, because the last commit loosened a test assertion.
